ctx.x: Well, among the things, back in the 20s, did most of them just think of something to go dance to and have a good time to it?

Well, I'm afraid we, no, Harold Bartell was more interested in our craft than others because he played the piano. And he played by ear like Steve who was Perron's piano player who was so well known. And in fact, Steve gave him lessons because he was interested in Harold. And I imagine, and of course my sister and I who sang a lot, were interested in the harmonizing part of it. But most of them, I would say, were not as devoted in jazz clubs as Menville and Susha and all of them are today. It was so comparatively…
What about, you know what you said, they didn't think of it as an art form.
